topic: Modes of Reproduction in Flowering and Non-Flowering Plants
key_concepts: Flowering plants reproduce sexually through pollination and fertilization and produce seed
Non-flowering plants such as ferns and mosses reproduce by spores
Ferns have fronds with sori on the underside that release spores
Mosses produce spore cases at the top that burst open and release spores
Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma
Cross-pollination transfers pollen to a flower of another plant of the same kind while sel
A pollen tube grows from the stigma down the style into the ovary where sperm fertilizes t
After fertilization the ovary swells, petals wilt, and seeds develop
A seed contains a seed coat, hilum, embryo, and cotyledon
Mongo seeds are dicots with two cotyledons while corn seeds are monocots with one cotyledo
Germination begins when seeds absorb water and the embryo grows into a new plant
Mosses and ferns can reproduce both sexually and asexually
